source_text: Verum, ut primum respirare licuit, consilium erat, quantum maxime tulisset ipsius rei natura, breviter promissa complere, nisi me actuosiorem denuo ingredi provinciam, beatissime pater Flore, voluisses; qui, quoniam tantum vales reverentia sanctitatis, ut praeceptis tuis segniter oboedire irreligiosum iudicem, obtinuisti facile ut in longiores vias compendium illius, quam elegeram, brevitatis extenderem. Favebis itaque operi tua auctoritate suscepto, cuius ob hoc potissimum nomen inserui, ut stilus securior et hilarior graderetur sub tantae patrocinio iussionis. Fuit igitur concepta animo non importuna ratio brevitatis; quia in illis quattuor libris cuncta fere, quae inventa a Manichaeis Augustini contra nos fuerant ore prolata, catholicae fidei veritas, pro qua et cum qua labentis mundi odia promeremur, tam disputationibus invictis, quam sacrae Legis testimoniis armata, protriverat, nec quidquam pene reliquum erat, si aequis iudicibus uteremur.
pass_a_gloss: But as soon as it was allowed to breathe, the plan was, as far as the nature of the matter itself would most bear, to complete the promises briefly, unless you, most blessed father Florus, had wanted me to enter again a more laborious province; you who, since you avail so much by reverence of holiness that I judge it irreligious to obey your precepts sluggishly, easily obtained that I should stretch into longer roads that shortcut of brevity which I had chosen. You will therefore favor a work taken up by your authority, whose name I have inserted chiefly for this, that the pen may walk more secure and more cheerful under the patronage of so great a command. There was therefore conceived in the mind a not unfitting reason of brevity; because in those four books the truth of the catholic faith, for which and with which we earn the hatreds of a sliding world, armed both with unconquered disputations and with testimonies of the sacred Law, had crushed almost all things which, invented by the Manichaeans, had been brought forth by Augustine's mouth against us, and almost nothing was left remaining, if we were using fair judges.

pass_b_english: As soon as I had room to breathe, however, I intended to fulfill my promises as briefly as the subject itself would allow. But you, most blessed Father Florus, wanted me to undertake a more demanding task once again. Your holiness commands such reverence that I consider it irreligious to obey your instructions sluggishly; you therefore had little difficulty persuading me to lengthen the short route I had chosen. Give your support, then, to a work undertaken at your command. I have placed your name in it chiefly so that my pen may advance more confidently and cheerfully under the protection of so weighty an instruction. There was a sound reason for the brevity I had planned. In those four books, the truth of the catholic faith, for which and with which we incur the hatred of a world in decline, had crushed almost everything invented by the Manichaeans and spoken against us by Augustine. Armed both with unanswerable arguments and with the testimony of the sacred Law, it had left almost nothing outstanding, if only we had fair judges.
